newsitem.title: FRANCE: INSTANT VIEW - Bank of France cuts interest rates.
newsitem.headline: INSTANT VIEW - Bank of France cuts interest rates.

text.p: Following are analysts' comments on the announcement of a cut in the French intervention and five-to-10 day rates after a meeting of the Bank of France monetary policy council on Tuesday.
JEAN-LOUIS MOURIER, ECONOMIST, LOUIS DREYFUS FINANCE:

It's a surprise all the same. I think the objective is to close in on German rates but I do not think this is a victory for the thesis of ("dove" council members Paul) Marchelli and (Jean-Pierre) Gerard.
Signs are that the Bundesbank will not raise rates in the near term. It's a good signal.
This is a very good sign the Bank of France is sending us. It's really telling us it's happy with the stability pact, which nobody doubted, but it shows they've resumed easing.
Some people are saying they will go through German rates, which I do not believe at all, but they will move toward German rates, the question is how fast.
As long as people don't believe this is the start of a devaluation, which I don't believe for a moment, it could have a positive effect on markets.
SEAN SHEPLEY, INTERNATIONAL ECONOMIST, CS FIRST BOSTON

Well I suppose the initial speculation may be that this signals a Bundesbank ease (on Thursday). The more likely speculation when people sit back will be that if the Bank of France has done this now it means they don't seriously expect the Bundesbank to do anything.
From a French domestic point of view it's not very interesting as it doesn't represent a change in policy.
The French situation could change if the Bundesbank doesn't cut, Chirac gets fed up and appoints doves onto the monetary committee and then we could have the Bank of France changing tack.
I think the risk of France going off on its own is one of the reasons the Bundesbank will cut (the repo rate)
